stem: A recipient calls reporting blood in emesis after discharge. According to urgent-contact education, how should the coordinator classify this symptom?

options.text: An urgent matter because oral bleeding is a potential source requiring prompt team contact
A non-urgent matter to address at the next routine refill call
An expected finding that never requires transplant team notification
A reason to permanently stop all immunosuppression without team guidance

explanation.rationale_correct: Bleeding from oral sources such as emesis is listed among urgent matters requiring prompt transplant team contact, alongside wound, rectal, and ostomy bleeding sources.

rationale_incorrect.B: Bleeding symptoms are urgent, not deferred to routine refill calls.
rationale_incorrect.C: Post-transplant teaching requires reporting bleeding from oral and other listed sources.
rationale_incorrect.D: Urgent bleeding prompts team evaluation rather than unilateral immunosuppression cessation.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 3, Patient Education → h. Communication → iii. Urgent matters → Bleeding

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 3 → h. Communication with the transplant team → iii. Urgent matters → Bleeding (oral/emesis source listed); PDF p. 111 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 030700 item; oral-bleeding urgent angle distinct from chest pain, rectal bleeding, stroke, infection, and shortness of breath items; anchor verified on Cupples p. 111.

stem: A liver transplant recipient develops fever and right upper quadrant tenderness. Laboratory results show elevated bilirubin, transaminases, and alkaline phosphatase. Which abnormality pattern is MOST consistent with cholangitis?

options.text: Fever with elevated bilirubin, transaminases, and alkaline phosphatase
Stable liver enzymes with isolated hypoglycemia only
Normal bilirubin with rising serum sodium as the sole abnormality
Isolated leukopenia without fever or abdominal symptoms

explanation.rationale_correct: Cholangitis may present with fever, right upper quadrant pain and tenderness, and laboratory findings including leukocytosis, elevated bilirubin, transaminases, and alkaline phosphatase.

rationale_incorrect.B: Cholangitis is associated with cholestatic and hepatocellular enzyme elevations, not isolated hypoglycemia alone.
rationale_incorrect.C: Elevated bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase are characteristic of cholangitis rather than isolated sodium changes.
rationale_incorrect.D: Cholangitis commonly presents with fever and abdominal symptoms; leukopenia alone is not the described pattern.

primary_anchor.section: Ch. 5, Infectious Diseases → b. Cholangitis → iv.

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → b. Cholangitis → iv. Laboratory findings (elevated bilirubin, transaminases, alkaline phosphatase); PDF p. 228 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 030100 item; liver cholangitis lab pattern distinct from kidney urinary leak (cctc-3034) and liver LFT rejection monitoring (cctc-3025); anchor verified on Cupples p. 228.

stem: A liver recipient with suspected cholangitis has imaging confirming biliary tree obstruction. What management approach aligns with standard post-transplant complication references?

options.text: Endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with dilatation when obstruction is present
Permanent cessation of all antibiotics regardless of biliary flow
No intervention because biliary obstruction never occurs after liver transplant
Immediate cessation of all immunosuppression without biliary evaluation

explanation.rationale_correct: In the setting of biliary tree obstruction, cholangitis treatment includes endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography with dilatation; intravenous antibiotics are used when biliary flow is adequate.

rationale_incorrect.B: Antimicrobial therapy is part of cholangitis management alongside biliary drainage when obstruction is present.
rationale_incorrect.C: Biliary obstruction is a recognized complication requiring intervention after liver transplantation.
rationale_incorrect.D: Management addresses biliary obstruction and infection; immunosuppression is not unilaterally stopped without team evaluation.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: biliary tree obstruction: endoscopic cholangiopancreatography (ERCP) with dilatation

references.citation: Core Curriculum for Transplant Nurses, 2nd ed. (Cupples et al., 2016).
references.locator: Ch. 5 → b. Cholangitis → 6. Treatment → b.ii. (ERCP with dilatation when biliary obstruction present); PDF p. 228 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Sixth 030200 item; liver cholangitis management angle distinct from kidney urinary leak (cctc-3035) and rejection fever (cctc-3026); anchor verified on Cupples p. 228.

stem: After a solid-organ transplant, when must a transplant hospital submit organ-specific transplant recipient follow-up (TRF) data to meet OPTN timely data requirements?

options.text: Within 90 days after the six-month and annual transplant anniversaries
Only on the day of initial waitlist registration
Within 1 day of every routine medication refill request
Never; TRF forms are optional for transplant hospitals

explanation.rationale_correct: OPTN Policy 18 requires transplant hospitals to submit organ-specific transplant recipient follow-up (TRF) within 90 days after the six-month and annual anniversary of the transplant date until death, graft failure, or planned graft removal.

rationale_incorrect.B: Waitlist registration triggers TCR submission, not TRF; TRF follows transplant anniversaries.
rationale_incorrect.C: Medication refill requests are not the TRF submission trigger.
rationale_incorrect.D: TRF is a required timely data instrument for followed recipients.

primary_anchor.quote_hint: 90 days after the six-month and annual anniversary of the transplant date

references.locator: Policy 18.1 → Data Submission Requirements (organ-specific transplant recipient follow-up [TRF] within 90 days after six-month and annual anniversaries); PDF p. 330 (repo file-page index; printed margin may differ).

notes: Source-first item. Fifth 030800 item; TRF timing distinct from TRR (cctc-3027), TCR (cctc-3036), UNet fields (cctc-3019), and SRTR aggregation (cctc-3005); anchor verified on optn-policies p. 330.
